cards.title: Global warming
cards.text: Global warming is the rise in Earth’s average temperature mainly because greenhouse gases from burning fuels trap heat.

qs.q: Global warming is mainly caused by…

cards.title: Greenhouse effect
cards.text: Gases like carbon dioxide trap heat in the atmosphere, a bit like a blanket around Earth.

qs.q: Which gas is the main driver of warming?

cards.title: Effects of warming
cards.text: Warming causes melting ice, rising seas, heatwaves, floods and droughts.

qs.q: A result of global warming is…

cards.title: Main causes of air pollution
cards.text: Vehicles, factories, burning waste and crop stubble, and construction dust are major causes of air pollution.

qs.q: A major cause of air pollution is…

cards.title: Effects of air pollution
cards.text: Polluted air causes asthma, heart disease, eye irritation and shorter lives.

cards.title: Reducing air pollution
cards.text: Use public transport, cycle, switch to clean energy, plant trees and avoid burning waste.

qs.q: One way to cut air pollution is…

cards.title: Water pollution
cards.text: Sewage, factory waste and plastic make rivers unsafe. Dirty water spreads disease and kills fish.

cards.title: Plastic problem
cards.text: Plastic lasts for hundreds of years, harms wildlife and ends up in oceans as tiny microplastics.

cards.title: Three Rs
cards.text: Reduce, reuse, recycle, in that order. Cutting waste matters most.

qs.q: Which of the 3 Rs matters most?

cards.title: Reducing waste
cards.text: Carry cloth bags, refuse single-use items, repair things and compost kitchen scraps.

qs.q: A good way to cut waste is…

cards.title: Wet and dry waste
cards.text: Separate kitchen waste (wet) from paper, plastic and metal (dry). It makes composting and recycling possible.

cards.title: Noise pollution
cards.text: Loud traffic and speakers cause stress, poor sleep and hearing loss.

cards.title: Soil pollution
cards.text: Chemicals and plastic in soil lower crop quality and enter our food.

cards.title: Deforestation
cards.text: Cutting forests destroys homes of wildlife, increases floods and removes trees that absorb carbon dioxide.

cards.title: Mitigation vs adaptation
cards.text: Mitigation cuts the causes of climate change. Adaptation helps us cope with its effects.

cards.title: Climate justice
cards.text: Poorer people contribute least to climate change yet often suffer most. Fairness matters in solutions.

cards.title: Floods and droughts
cards.text: Climate change makes rainfall extreme: too much in some places, too little in others.

cards.title: Heatwaves
cards.text: Heatwaves are becoming more frequent. Drink water, avoid noon sun and check on the elderly.

options: Drink water and avoid noon sun

cards.title: Rising seas
cards.text: Melting ice and warming oceans raise sea levels, threatening coastal cities and islands.

cards.title: Early warning
cards.text: Satellite forecasts and alerts let authorities evacuate people before cyclones and save lives.

qs.q: What helps move people to safety before a cyclone?

cards.title: Climate refugees
cards.text: When land floods or dries up, people are forced to move. This is a growing human problem.

cards.title: Carbon footprint
cards.text: Your carbon footprint is the greenhouse gas your lifestyle produces, from travel, food and electricity.

cards.title: Cutting our footprint
cards.text: Save electricity, walk or cycle, eat local food and waste less to cut your footprint.

qs.q: A way to reduce carbon footprint is…

cards.title: Coral and ocean
cards.text: Warm, acidic oceans bleach coral reefs, which shelter many sea creatures.

cards.title: Glaciers
cards.text: Himalayan glaciers feed major rivers. If they shrink, millions may lose water security.

cards.title: Disaster preparedness
cards.text: Knowing evacuation routes, keeping emergency kits and learning first aid reduces harm in disasters.

cards.title: Climate agreements
cards.text: Countries make agreements to cut emissions together because the atmosphere is shared by all.

qs.q: Why do countries agree on emissions?

cards.title: Sustainable development
cards.text: Meeting today’s needs without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs.

cards.title: Renewable vs fossil
cards.text: Renewables like sun, wind and water never run out. Fossil fuels such as coal and oil are limited and polluting.

cards.title: Solar power
cards.text: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity with no smoke. India gets lots of sunshine, so solar suits it.

cards.title: Nuclear energy
cards.text: It gives large low-carbon power but needs careful waste storage and strict safety.

qs.q: A challenge of nuclear power is…

cards.title: Why forests matter
cards.text: Forests absorb carbon dioxide, hold soil, bring rain and shelter wildlife.

cards.title: Biodiversity
cards.text: Biodiversity is the variety of life on Earth. When species vanish, ecosystems weaken.

cards.title: Conservation
cards.text: Conservation means protecting nature, from forests and rivers to animals, so it lasts.

cards.title: Save water
cards.text: Fix leaks, harvest rainwater, close taps and reuse water for plants.

cards.title: Public transport
cards.text: Buses, metros and trains move many people with less pollution per person than private cars.

qs.q: Which is more eco-friendly per person?

cards.title: Energy saving
cards.text: Switch off unused lights, use LED bulbs and efficient appliances to cut electricity use.

cards.title: Individual vs collective
cards.text: One person’s change is small but millions together make big impact, along with government action.

cards.title: Green economy
cards.text: Green jobs in solar, recycling and conservation show that growth and nature can go together.

qs.q: A green job is one in…
